data.title: Cross-Application Identity Collision — Same Biometric or Device Across Different Identities
data.description: Detects the same biometric template (face embedding), device fingerprint, or behavioral pattern appearing across applications submitted under different identity names. Fraudsters using AI-generated faces may reuse the same base model or device, creating detectable collisions in the biometric or device space. Even when AI-generated facial images appear visually distinct, the underlying face embedding vectors may cluster due to shared generative model artifacts. Similarly, device fingerprints and behavioral biometric profiles persist across sessions even when the presented identity changes, enabling cross-application correlation that reveals synthetic identity networks.

detection.condition: selection_application AND (same face_embedding_hash across 2+ different applicant_name/ssn_hash combinations within 90 days) OR (same device_fingerprint across 2+ different applicant_name/ssn_hash combinations within 90 days)

enrichment_required.source: Biometric verification — locality-sensitive hash of facial embedding vector
Biometric verification — cosine similarity between face embeddings across applications
Behavioral biometrics — hash of behavioral pattern (typing, mouse movement, scroll)

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Cross-Application Identity Collision Detection
// Detects same biometric or device across different identity applications
event_type="CREDIT_APPLICATION"
| application_date > now() - 90d
| groupBy(face_embedding_hash, function=[
    count(distinct=true, field=applicant_name, as=distinct_names),
    count(distinct=true, field=ssn_hash, as=distinct_ssns),
    collect([applicant_id, applicant_name, ssn_hash, application_date,
             device_fingerprint], limit=50) as application_details
  ])
| distinct_names >= 2 OR distinct_ssns >= 2
| identity_collision_type := "biometric_collision"
| select([face_embedding_hash, distinct_names, distinct_ssns,
          identity_collision_type, application_details])
| sort(distinct_names, order=desc)

`comment("Splunk SPL for Cross-Application Identity Collision Detection")`
`comment("Detects same biometric or device across different identity applications")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:document_verification
  event_type="CREDIT_APPLICATION"
  earliest=-90d@d
| stats
    dc(applicant_name) as distinct_names,
    dc(ssn_hash) as distinct_ssns,
    values(applicant_id) as applicant_ids,
    values(applicant_name) as names,
    values(ssn_hash) as ssn_hashes,
    values(application_date) as application_dates
    by face_embedding_hash
| where distinct_names >= 2 OR distinct_ssns >= 2
| eval identity_collision_type = "biometric_collision"
| append [
    search index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:document_verification
      event_type="CREDIT_APPLICATION"
      earliest=-90d@d
    | stats
        dc(applicant_name) as distinct_names,
        dc(ssn_hash) as distinct_ssns,
        values(applicant_id) as applicant_ids,
        values(applicant_name) as names,
        values(ssn_hash) as ssn_hashes,
        values(application_date) as application_dates
        by device_fingerprint
    | where distinct_names >= 2 OR distinct_ssns >= 2
    | eval identity_collision_type = "device_collision"
  ]
| sort - distinct_names
queries.sql:
-- SQL for Cross-Application Identity Collision Detection
-- Detects same biometric or device across different identity applications
-- Part 1: Biometric collisions (same face_embedding_hash, different identities)
SELECT
  'biometric_collision' AS identity_collision_type,
  a.face_embedding_hash AS collision_key,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_name) AS distinct_names,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.ssn_hash) AS distinct_ssns,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.applicant_name, ', ') AS names,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.applicant_id, ', ') AS applicant_ids,
  MIN(a.application_date) AS earliest_application,
  MAX(a.application_date) AS latest_application
FROM credit_applications a
WHERE a.event_type = 'CREDIT_APPLICATION'
  AND a.application_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND a.face_embedding_hash IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.face_embedding_hash
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_name) >= 2
   OR COUNT(DISTINCT a.ssn_hash) >= 2

UNION ALL

-- Part 2: Device collisions (same device_fingerprint, different identities)
SELECT
  'device_collision' AS identity_collision_type,
  a.device_fingerprint AS collision_key,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_name) AS distinct_names,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.ssn_hash) AS distinct_ssns,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.applicant_name, ', ') AS names,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT a.applicant_id, ', ') AS applicant_ids,
  MIN(a.application_date) AS earliest_application,
  MAX(a.application_date) AS latest_application
FROM credit_applications a
WHERE a.event_type = 'CREDIT_APPLICATION'
  AND a.application_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND a.device_fingerprint IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.device_fingerprint
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.applicant_name) >= 2
   OR COUNT(DISTINCT a.ssn_hash) >= 2

ORDER BY distinct_names DESC

references: Federal Reserve Board, Synthetic Identity Fraud in the U.S. Payment System (2024)
Entrust 2025 Identity Fraud Report — cross-platform identity correlation
LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Global State of Fraud and Identity Report 2026
falsepositives: Household members applying from the same shared device (device collision only)
Identical twins or family members with similar facial features (biometric collision)
Corporate devices used by loan officers submitting multiple client applications
